title: ao.break-glass-record/v1
description: One break-glass merge-authority use, recorded as an auditable artifact (kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1276). The merge right to master lives with ONE queue identity; the named break-glass actor is the only other principal, and every use of it must leave this record: who used it, why, for which pull request, inside which time-box, which channel the owner was paged on, and who acknowledged the page. Enforced by governance/platform/break-glass/validate.py (stdlib-only subset validator: the schema is the single source of truth for the shape, the validator adds the cross-field checks a schema cannot express) and refused by name by scripts/check-merge-identity.sh.

schema.description: The record's own identity. A record whose schema string is anything else is refused by name.

id.description: Minted by scripts/branch-protection.sh break-glass: bg-<UTC date>T<UTC time>Z-<hex>. It is also the name of the file under records/, so a use and its record resolve to each other by one id.

at.description: When the break-glass authority was taken (UTC, second resolution).

actor.description: The principal that used the break-glass right. scripts/check-merge-identity.sh refuses a record whose actor is not the actor the declaration names (record-actor-not-declared).

principal_expected.description: The queue identity that normally holds the merge right. Naming it on the record is what makes a bypass a measured exception rather than an unstated drift from the declaration.

pr.description: The pull request merged under break-glass, or null for a direct push with no pull request (the case this issue exists to make visible).

reason.description: Why the queue identity could not be used. A short reason is refused by name: an unexplained bypass cannot be reviewed after the fact.

expires_at.description: The break-glass right is time-boxed: the validator refuses a record whose expiry is not after its start (record-expiry-not-after-start) and one whose window exceeds the declared ceiling.

paged.description: The page to the owner. A record without it is refused by name, so 'break-glass pages the owner' is evidence rather than intention.

channel.description: Where the page went (a notice id, a mailbox directive, a chat channel).

ack_by.description: The owner who acknowledged the page. A page nobody acknowledged is an escalation that did not land (the failure governance/notices was built for, #1269).

evidence.description: The command output, commit or url the use can be checked against.
